Legal Memorandum: Breach of Exclusive Distribution Agreement

Client: Distribuidora Atlântica Ltda., limited liability company, São Paulo, Brazil
Opposing Party: Viña Cordillera S.A., corporation, Santiago, Chile
Practice Area: International Arbitration; Commercial Litigation; Intellectual Property
Industry: Wine Industry; Food and Beverage; Import and Export
Governing Law: United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods; Chilean law
Dispute Resolution: ICC arbitration, three arbitrators, seat Lima, Peru
Claims: breach of contract; breach of warranty; wrongful termination; trademark infringement; unfair competition
Remedies Sought: direct damages; consequential damages; lost profits; prejudgment interest; preliminary injunction; accounting of profits

Background
Exclusive Distribution Agreement, five-year contract term. Supplier warranty: product specifications, certificate of origin, Brazilian import regulations, food safety regulations, labeling requirements. Payment: invoice, letter of credit, commercial bank, payment term, bill of lading.
Customs detention: Brazilian customs authority detained wine shipment; laboratory reports showed regulatory violation. Ministry of Agriculture administrative order: product recall; customs duties; regulatory fine; storage costs.
Supplier terminated Agreement without notice; appointed competing distributor, Rio de Janeiro; continued trademark license to competitor.

Legal Issues
1. Fundamental breach of contract: nonconforming goods, Article 25 CISG.
2. Wrongful termination without cause: notice period; exclusivity clause.
3. Damages: direct damages, consequential damages, lost profits, prejudgment interest; limitation of liability clause.
4. Interim relief: arbitral tribunal; emergency arbitrator; trademark infringement; unfair competition.

Analysis
Breach of contract and breach of warranty: laboratory reports, customs detention records, recall order establish nonconforming goods. Buyer remedies: declare contract avoided; claim damages; restitution of purchase price. Timely notice of nonconformity defeats waiver defense.
Wrongful termination: termination clause requires material breach, written notice, thirty-day cure period. Competing distributor appointment breaches exclusivity clause and implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing.
Damages: expectation damages, lost profits, contract term; expert testimony, forensic accountant; incidental damages, regulatory fine. Limitation of liability clause excludes gross negligence and willful misconduct. Force majeure clause: no defense.
Intellectual property: trademark sublicense, Brazil; likelihood of confusion; trademark infringement; unfair competition; accounting of profits.
Jurisdiction and procedure: arbitration clause, New York Convention; arbitral award enforcement, Brazil, Chile, Peru. ICC Rules: emergency arbitrator, interim measures. Brazilian court: preliminary injunction in aid of arbitration.
Defenses and risks: counterclaim, unpaid invoices, USD 480,000; statute of limitations defense; jurisdictional objection. Rebuttal evidence: documentary evidence, witness statements, chain of custody. Confidentiality clause; data protection; Brazil General Data Protection Law (LGPD); Chile personal data protection law; protective order; discovery.

Recommendations
1. Request for Arbitration, ICC; filing fee.
2. Emergency arbitrator application; injunction.
3. Litigation hold; electronically stored information.
4. Damages expert witness; food safety expert witness.
5. Mediation; settlement agreement; release; indemnification clause; non-disparagement clause.

sentence_pos.text: Legal Memorandum:

Breach of Exclusive Distribution Agreement

Client: Distribuidora Atlântica Ltda., limited liability company, São Paulo, Brazil
Opposing Party: Viña Cordillera S.A., corporation, Santiago, Chile
Practice Area: International Arbitration; Commercial Litigation; Intellectual Property
Industry: Wine Industry; Food and Beverage; Import and Export
Governing Law: United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods; Chilean law
Dispute Resolution: ICC arbitration, three arbitrators, seat Lima, Peru
Claims: breach of contract; breach of warranty; wrongful termination; trademark infringement; unfair competition
Remedies Sought: direct damages; consequential damages; lost profits; prejudgment interest; preliminary injunction; accounting of profits

Background
Exclusive Distribution Agreement, five-year contract term.
Supplier warranty: product specifications, certificate of origin, Brazilian import regulations, food safety regulations, labeling requirements.
Payment: invoice, letter of credit, commercial bank, payment term, bill of lading.
Customs detention: Brazilian customs authority detained wine shipment; laboratory reports showed regulatory violation.
Ministry of Agriculture administrative order: product recall; customs duties; regulatory fine; storage costs.
Supplier terminated Agreement without notice; appointed competing distributor, Rio de Janeiro; continued trademark license to competitor.

Legal Issues
1.
Fundamental breach of contract: nonconforming goods, Article 25 CISG.
2. Wrongful termination without cause: notice period; exclusivity clause.
Damages: direct damages, consequential damages, lost profits, prejudgment interest; limitation of liability clause.
Interim relief: arbitral tribunal; emergency arbitrator; trademark infringement; unfair competition.

Analysis
Breach of contract and breach of warranty: laboratory reports, customs detention records, recall order establish nonconforming goods.
Buyer remedies: declare contract avoided; claim damages; restitution of purchase price.
Timely notice of nonconformity defeats waiver defense.
Wrongful termination: termination clause requires material breach, written notice, thirty-day cure period.
Competing distributor appointment breaches exclusivity clause and implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing.
Damages: expectation damages, lost profits, contract term; expert testimony, forensic accountant; incidental damages, regulatory fine.
Limitation of liability clause excludes gross negligence and willful misconduct.
Force majeure clause: no defense.
Intellectual property: trademark sublicense, Brazil; likelihood of confusion; trademark infringement; unfair competition; accounting of profits.
Jurisdiction and procedure: arbitration clause, New York Convention; arbitral award enforcement, Brazil, Chile, Peru.
ICC Rules: emergency arbitrator, interim measures.

Brazilian court: preliminary injunction in aid of arbitration.
Defenses and risks: counterclaim, unpaid invoices, USD 480,000; statute of limitations defense; jurisdictional objection.
Rebuttal evidence: documentary evidence, witness statements, chain of custody.
Confidentiality clause; data protection; Brazil General Data Protection Law (LGPD);
Chile personal data protection law; protective order; discovery.

Recommendations
1. Request for Arbitration, ICC; filing fee.
Emergency arbitrator application; injunction.
Litigation hold; electronically stored information.
Damages expert witness; food safety expert witness.
Mediation; settlement agreement; release; indemnification clause; non-disparagement clause.

Legal Memorandum: Breach of Exclusive Distribution Agreement

Client: Distribuidora Atlântica Ltda., limited liability company, São Paulo, Brazil
Opposing Party: Viña Cordillera S.A., corporation, Santiago, Chile
Practice Area: International Arbitration; Commercial Litigation; Intellectual Property
Industry: Wine Industry; Food and Beverage; Import and Export
Governing Law: United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods; Chilean law
Dispute Resolution: ICC arbitration, three arbitrators, seat Lima, Peru
Claims: breach of contract; breach of warranty; wrongful termination; trademark infringement; unfair competition
Remedies Sought: direct damages; consequential damages; lost profits; prejudgment interest; preliminary injunction; accounting of profits

Background
Exclusive Distribution Agreement, five-year contract term. Supplier warranty: product specifications, certificate of origin, Brazilian import regulations, food safety regulations, labeling requirements. Payment: invoice, letter of credit, commercial bank, payment term, bill of lading.
Customs detention: Brazilian customs authority detained wine shipment; laboratory reports showed regulatory violation. Ministry of Agriculture administrative order: product recall; customs duties; regulatory fine; storage costs.
Supplier terminated Agreement without notice; appointed competing distributor, Rio de Janeiro; continued trademark license to competitor.

Legal Issues
1. Fundamental breach of contract: nonconforming goods, Article 25 CISG.
2. Wrongful termination without cause: notice period; exclusivity clause.
3. Damages: direct damages, consequential damages, lost profits, prejudgment interest; limitation of liability clause.
4. Interim relief: arbitral tribunal; emergency arbitrator; trademark infringement; unfair competition.

Analysis
Breach of contract and breach of warranty: laboratory reports, customs detention records, recall order establish nonconforming goods. Buyer remedies: declare contract avoided; claim damages; restitution of purchase price. Timely notice of nonconformity defeats waiver defense.
Wrongful termination: termination clause requires material breach, written notice, thirty-day cure period. Competing distributor appointment breaches exclusivity clause and implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing.
Damages: expectation damages, lost profits, contract term; expert testimony, forensic accountant; incidental damages, regulatory fine. Limitation of liability clause excludes gross negligence and willful misconduct. Force majeure clause: no defense.
Intellectual property: trademark sublicense, Brazil; likelihood of confusion; trademark infringement; unfair competition; accounting of profits.
Jurisdiction and procedure: arbitration clause, New York Convention; arbitral award enforcement, Brazil, Chile, Peru. ICC Rules: emergency arbitrator, interim measures. Brazilian court: preliminary injunction in aid of arbitration.
Defenses and risks: counterclaim, unpaid invoices, USD 480,000; statute of limitations defense; jurisdictional objection. Rebuttal evidence: documentary evidence, witness statements, chain of custody. Confidentiality clause; data protection; Brazil General Data Protection Law (LGPD); Chile personal data protection law; protective order; discovery.

Recommendations
1. Request for Arbitration, ICC; filing fee.
2. Emergency arbitrator application; injunction.
3. Litigation hold; electronically stored information.
4. Damages expert witness; food safety expert witness.
5. Mediation; settlement agreement; release; indemnification clause; non-disparagement clause.
